title: OpenCode harness lane table
description: The jobs a fleet can hand out. A lane says what it is for and nothing about models: a profile says which lanes it enables and which model serves each one. The lane table is the single list of lane names in the kit; `src/profile.js` reads it, `src/config.js` compiles it into the generated config, and `profiles/schema.json` must name the same lanes.

propertyNames.description: A lane name is a slug: it becomes an agent name, a prompt filename and a permission key.

mode.description: A primary agent is one a person talks to and that may delegate; a subagent is one that is only ever handed a job. OpenCode's own `AgentConfig.mode` allows a third value, `all`, which this kit does not use.

description.description: When to use this lane. The model reads it on every turn to choose a lane, so it has to be long enough to select on and different enough from the others not to overlap. Two lanes that sound alike are the failure mode of a large catalogue, not a large catalogue itself.

steps.description: Maximum agentic iterations before the lane is forced to answer in prose. A runaway lane reports instead of looping.

permission.description: Per-lane permission rules, merged over the ones already on the agent. A read-only lane sets `edit: deny`; a lane that runs commands lists them.

prompt.description: The lane's instructions, relative to the kit root. The prompt body lives in a file, not in this table and not in the generated config, because an agent markdown file of the same name replaces the config entry wholesale.
